subject: Clarify DPA: model improvement prohibition + subprocessor geofencing
messages:
From: Jen Park <jen.park@healthecho.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on DPA wording around model improvement and where subprocessors will be placed

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the call earlier. Legal asked me to get a short written summary so they can propose precise redlines. The requirements they flagged:

- We need a contractual commitment that Healthecho data (including prompts & responses) will not be used to improve models or for any model training, adaptive learning, or benchmarking unless we opt in explicitly.
- We also need the ability to restrict subprocessors to a geography (EU-only or US-only) for particular workloads and a clear path to evidence (attestation + onshore KMS where required).
- Lastly, they want clarity on ownership of prompt/response outputs — specifically whether outputs generated from our inputs are licensed back to us or retained by Redwood for service improvement.

I've attached the DPA excerpt they propose (Healthecho_DPA_excerpt.pdf). Can you confirm what operational controls Redwood can offer, and a short list of proposed contract language we could give to Legal?

Appreciate a short bullet reply if possible — Legal is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Jen
Jen Park
Head of Security & Privacy
Healthecho

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA wording around model improvement and where subprocessors will be placed

Hi Jen —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up-front and then I will let David add operational detail. Short answer: yes, we can offer an explicit model-improvement exclusion plus subprocessor geofencing options. We can also provide an evidence pack and onshore KMS integrations.

Suggested next steps:
- David to propose precise operational artifacts and an implementation SLA for geofencing.
- We propose contract language for a DPA addendum that: (a) prohibits model training on Healthecho data unless you opt in; (b) grants Healthecho exclusive output licensing for its generated outputs; (c) specifies subprocessor geofences and evidence delivery cadence.
- If that looks okay, we’ll prep the evidence pack (SOC 2 + subprocessor inventory + ops playbook) and a draft addendum.

I’ve looped in David and Karthik for technical and legal/contract phrasing.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Field Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jen Park <jen.park@healthecho.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA wording around model improvement and where subprocessors will be placed

Jen —

Thanks — below are concrete operational options and suggested contract snippets. High-level: we can offer a "no-model-improvement" mode per tenant plus per-workload subprocessor geofencing. Important constraints/notes included.

Operational controls (what we can deliver):
1) Tenant-level model-improvement exclusion (NO_IMPROVE flag): once enabled, ingestion paths are tagged and excluded from any training/finetune pipelines. Data remains available for inference only. Applies to prompts, responses, logs, and ephemeral KV unless explicitly retained by you.

2) Short TTL ephemeral KV and optional prompt redaction: For the most sensitive paths we can configure ephemeral KV cache TTLs (<1 hour) and automatic redaction of structured fields (SSNs, PII patterns) prior to being written to logs.

3) Subprocessor geofencing: We operate regional pools. For EU geofence requests we commit to routing inference and storage to our EU-dedicated pools and to only use subprocessors contracted and whitelisted for that region. For onshore KMS we can restrict key material to specified regions and provide attestations.

4) Evidence & cadence: We can deliver an evidence pack containing SOC 2 Type II summary, subprocessor inventory (signed attestation), network flow diagrams showing regional routing, and a runbook excerpt describing the NO_IMPROVE enforcement. Delivery: initial pack within 7 business days after addendum execution; quarterly attestations thereafter.

Suggested contractual language (short):
- "Provider will not use Customer Data (including prompts and responses) to train, fine-tune, benchmark, or otherwise improve Provider's machine learning models, except to the extent Customer provides an explicit, auditable opt-in for specific datasets and defined time windows."
- "Customer retains exclusive license to Outputs generated from Customer Data. Provider shall not use Outputs for model training or product improvement absent Customer's prior written consent."
- "Provider will route Customer Data for Processing only to subprocessors and infrastructure pools described in Schedule X. For workloads marked by Customer as 'Regionally Restricted', Provider shall process and store such data exclusively within the specified geographic region and only via subprocessors that have executed region-specific attestations."

Operational caveats:
- Very large live-patching of models is prevented under NO_IMPROVE, but we cannot retroactively remove model weights if training on older snapshot data occurred prior to an agreement date — we will represent and warrant the cutover date.
- Some third-party telemetry (infrastructure monitoring) may still involve aggregated, non-identifiable metrics. We can exclude tenant IDs from telemetry in the restricted profile and include that in the attestation.

I'll attach our internal ops write-up that maps controls to evidence (redwood_no_train_ops.pdf). Happy to walk Legal through the specifics.

-David
David Kim
Director, Platform Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_no_train_ops.pdf (doc)
From: Jen Park <jen.park@healthecho.com>

Date: 2026-11-09T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA wording around model improvement and where subprocessors will be placed

Sean / David —

That is very helpful; thanks. A few clarifying asks from Legal:

- Can the contract language include a defined "Effective Exclusion Date" (we want a clear cutover timestamp, and a warranty that no retrospective training will occur on data received after that date)?
- For geofencing: Legal wants to see the list of subprocessors for the EU-only profile and a sample attestation. Is that part of the evidence pack or a separate deliverable?
- On outputs: they want a short definition clause for "Outputs" referencing prompts + model-generated text + structured derivations. Also they asked whether Redwood would accept an explicit license grant to Healthecho that is "exclusive for the purpose of productizing and sublicensing Outputs."

They've attached a redlined excerpt and a few comments in the PDF. We should aim for a version they can sign by EOD Monday if possible.

Jen
Jen Park
Head of Security & Privacy
Healthecho

Attachment: Healthecho_DPA_excerpt.pdf (with comments)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Jen Park <jen.park@healthecho.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA wording around model improvement and where subprocessors will be placed

Jen —

Good plan. Commitments from our side:

- We will include an "Effective Exclusion Date" in the addendum; we will warranty that no model updates using Healthecho data will occur after that timestamp and will provide a signed attestation.
- Subprocessor list for EU-only profile and a sample attestation will be included in the evidence pack. We will include onshore KMS options for key custody where requested.
- We can add an "Outputs" definition and a license clause. We need to confirm the exclusivity scope — in principle we can grant an exclusive license to Healthecho for Outputs for productization, but we will need carveouts for aggregated, deidentified analytics for internal monitoring unless you request exclusion in the addendum. David: can you confirm the exclusion language and any telemetry carveouts we need to highlight for Legal?

We will prepare: (1) DPA addendum draft with Effective Exclusion Date placeholder; (2) evidence pack (SOC 2 summary, subprocessor list + attestation, NO_IMPROVE ops doc); and (3) proposed Outputs license wording. Target: initial packet to Jen/legal by close of business Monday (2026-11-15).

Thanks all — I’ll follow up with a short action tracker.

Sean
Head of Field Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
